rv.q: It packs a lot of punch into a compact package, barely more than an hour long but weighing heavy on us by the end.
Somehow the Berliner Ensemble current director’s first New York premiere, it arrived with maxed-out anticipation (I’d never seen the lobby abuzz like that) and managed to exceed expectations.
The Swamp Dwellers makes these issues into exciting, beguiling theater.
Thank good fortune, though, it's here now in a handsome production, directed sure-handedly by Awoye Timpo.

Even six decades since its debut, The Swamp Dwellers still whispers truths to modern Western audiences — about family loyalty, the downsides of urbanization, the threat of environmental degradation, and the undue influence of corrupt religious figures.

cn.t: Soyinka's rarely-seen 1958 drama receives mostly positive reviews for its taut, mythic storytelling and handsome production, though one critic finds it less compelling. The off-Broadway debut impresses with sharp direction and strong performances.
